text:
support-lead: FYI customer ACME reporting a p99 jump starting ~09:12 UTC. They see a mix of 401s and 502s, and are seeing billing for attempts that failed. Ticket: https://redwood.support/t/ACME-4521 - can we triage?
ana: I can start digging into traces. 09:12 sounds like the canary we rolled for the continuous-batcher flags.
deploy-bot: rolled config 'continuous-batcher.v2' -> {"hold_ms": "150", "max_batch": "64", "coalesce_auth_headers": "true"} at 2025-11-18T09:12:03Z by release/eng-sre-canary
mike: putting the traces for ACME in APM. quick observation: a lot of 401s are within batches where the first item succeeds and subsequent items fail with "auth: header missing".
nana: exact log lines: "batcher: attach_auth header_index=0 ok; header_index=1 missing" and "auth: token-lookup mismatch for request_id=..."
nana: looks like when coalescing we are reusing the first request's auth index instead of mapping per-request headers. that would cause 401s for users with different tokens in same batch.
jordan: that would also cause clients to retry, inflating latency and token consumption -> billing headaches. good catch.
mike: repro script (small):
```bash
for i in {1..20}; do \
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN_$i" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/generate &
done; wait
```
send from a single host with high concurrency and small payloads (tiny prompts) to maximize coalescing. I reproduced locally: ~15% of requests returned 401 during the canary.
ashley: ACME is asking for immediate mitigation + credits. I told them we were investigating and would update in 15m.
jordan: immediate mitigation options:
- toggle off coalesce_auth_headers feature flag (safe)
- reduce hold_ms back to 20ms (reduce coalescing)
- route ACME to dedicated non-coalescing pool (if tenant pinning available)
Which is fastest?
ana: feature flag flip is fastest. patching configmap will apply cluster-wide though.
jordan: I can flip the FF via our feature gateway:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://ops.redwood/api/ff/continuous-batcher/coalesce_auth_headers" -d '{"enabled":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
```
I will also prepare a rollback to hold_ms=20.
sre-bot: alert: p99 latency for tenant ACME increased from 220ms -> 1.3s at 2025-11-18T09:12:10Z (matching canary). error-rate 401 increased x12.
jordan: done - feature flag toggled off. waiting for propagation (~30s).
infra-bot: feature flag propagation confirmed at 2025-11-18T09:12:48Z.
nana: running new traces now. initial look: 401s dropped to baseline. p99 falling.
mike: can we also check billing pipeline? why are they charged for failed attempts?
nana: billing logs show token_count increment happens at pre-processing before auth validation for short requests; we should file a follow-up. ACME was charged for the attempts that returned 401 because counting is before auth guard.
ashley: I've issued provisional credits for ACME and told them we disabled the flag and will follow up after postmortem.
jordan: action items:
- (P0) rollback coalesce_auth_headers (done) and set hold_ms=20 (will patch now).
- (P1) file bug: batching auth header mapping regression (assign to eng-runtime).
- (P2) billing: avoid counting failed auth attempts before validation (assign to finance infra).
- (P3) add e2e test to send mixed-Authorization headers in the same batch.
- (P4) postmortem + customer notes.

jordan: patching hold_ms now to 20ms: `kubectl -n redwood patch configmap continuous-batcher -p '{"data":{"hold_ms":"20"}}'`
infra-bot: configmap patched and rollout started at 2025-11-18T09:15:02Z (rolling restart of batcher pods).
sre-bot: metric check: p99 for ACME back to 240ms at 09:15:57Z; 401s back to baseline.
nana: confirming traces show no auth-mismatch after flag flip and hold_ms change.
mike: repro verification script now returns <1% 401 locally.
ashley: customer updated and credits applied. they accepted the temporary credits and asked for timeline for fix.
jordan: assigning runtime bug to @ana and @mike for immediate PR. I'll schedule postmortem for tomorrow 10:00.
nana: I'll own the runtime PR and include tests. initial fix: ensure per-request auth header mapping is preserved when coalescing; guardrails added.
sre-bot: reminder: please include trace IDs and sample failing request_ids in the postmortem doc.
support-lead: thanks team. great quick triage. we'll follow up with ACME and close ticket after the fix lands + verification. :thumbsup:
